title: Sell Mineral Rights in Monument, NM
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Monument, NM
metaDescription: Monument is an unincorporated Lea County community sitting on active San Andres and horizontal Bone Spring acreage near Hobbs. We buy mineral interests here directly.
heroLead: Monument isn't an incorporated town, it's a small unincorporated community, but the ground underneath it has been worked hard since the Hobbs field days.
intro: Because Monument never grew into a full municipality, most of what defines this area for a mineral owner is Draw Road and the surrounding sections rather than any city limits. The oil history is real, though, this sits close enough to the original Hobbs field area to share a lot of the same production story.

sections.heading: Unincorporated doesn't mean undeveloped
paragraphs: Don't let the lack of city limits fool you into thinking this area sees less activity. Monument-area acreage has both legacy San Andres wells from decades of shelf development and, closer to the Texas line, newer horizontal Bone Spring wells. We check both when we look at your tract.

sections.heading: Address and legal description mismatches
paragraphs: Because Monument isn't incorporated, mailing addresses on old division orders sometimes list Hobbs or Lovington instead, which can confuse an owner trying to confirm exactly where their interest sits. We work off the legal description, section, township, and range, not the mailing address, so this doesn't slow anything down.

sections.heading: Proximity to Hobbs matters more than the name
paragraphs: Monument sits close enough to Hobbs that a lot of the same production and permitting patterns apply, and operators active around Hobbs commonly hold acreage here too. We check the same range of San Andres and horizontal Bone Spring activity we'd check for a Hobbs tract when we look at Monument acreage.

faqs.question: Is Monument a real town with its own oil field?
faqs.answer: It's an unincorporated community rather than an incorporated town, close enough to the historic Hobbs field to share a similar production history. We identify your tract by its legal description rather than the community name.

faqs.question: My old division order lists Hobbs as my address, not Monument. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: No, that's common for unincorporated Lea County communities. We confirm your interest by section, township, and range, not the mailing address on the document.

faqs.question: What kind of wells are typically near Monument?
faqs.answer: A mix of older San Andres shelf wells and, toward the Texas line, newer horizontal Bone Spring wells. We check which applies to your specific tract before quoting.

faqs.question: Should I expect similar activity to Hobbs since Monument is so close?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, given the proximity and shared operator footprint. But we still confirm your tract's specific production and permit history rather than assuming it matches Hobbs exactly.
